clue.text: Shameless tirade released aboard vessel

indicators.note: something released is let go, so the word for the tirade is set free from the longer word

blocks.note: flagrant means blatant, openly shameless
a rant is a tirade
on board, as in on a ship

explanation.surface: Someone launches into an unashamed rant while on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Take RANT out of FLAGRANT to leave FLAG, then add ON. 'Vessel' suggests a boat, but it is a drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large jug or bottle for serving wine or ale, a kind of drinking vessel.

clue.text: Footballers topping table fuelled by street cuisine?

indicators.note: fuel is put into an engine, so the next piece goes inside the others

blocks.note: the FA is the Football Association
St is the abbreviation for street
to keep a good table is to serve good food

explanation.surface: Footballers top the league table, powered by food bought on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping table' sounds like heading a league, but FA simply goes on top of the word for table in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast food is quick, cheap takeaway fare of the kind sold on the street, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Course cockney isn't attending having run early

indicators.note: a cockney accent famously drops the h at the start of words, so that letter goes
R stands for run, and early means it shifts one place forward

blocks.note: isn't attending means ain't here in casual speech

explanation.surface: A cockney skips a race meeting, having gone for a run early.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops the h of here. Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a racecourse near Liverpool, home of the Grand National steeplechase.

clue.text: Drink Peronis essentially and agree to relax

indicators.note: essentially means at its heart, so only the central letter is kept
relaxing loosens things up, so these letters fall into a looser new order

blocks.note: the middle letter of a seven-letter word
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Friends agree to unwind over some Peroni beers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a link but is part of the letters to be rearranged. Peroni is an Italian lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a fizzy orange-flavoured soft drink.

clue.text: Improprieties of Conservative overwhelmed by flip-flops?

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed by something is to be swamped and surrounded by it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: flip-flops are an example of sandals, hence the question mark
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's wrongdoings are buried under a pile of U-turns, flip-flops being political changes of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flip-flops' suggests political U-turns, but here it is the summer footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandals are disgraceful actions or affairs that cause public outrage, so improper conduct.

clue.text: Waterworks that could produce cool cider?

indicators.note: the answer itself contains a word for ripping apart, and producing the phrase means the letters are being shaken into it

blocks.note: taken as written; the solver reverses the process
the word in the answer that, read as rips, works the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A tearful outburst that might be soothed with a chilled glass of cider.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the answer read as an instruction, CROCODILE tears (rips up), makes COOL CIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterworks is slang for crying, and crocodile tears are a show of insincere weeping.

clue.text: I won't put up full marks, maybe score of nine?

indicators.note: in a down answer, putting something up means reading it from bottom to top

blocks.note: no is a refusal
ten out of ten is full marks

explanation.surface: A judge refuses to award a perfect ten, perhaps giving only nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests marks, but it is a musical score written for nine players.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a musical composition for nine instruments or voices, so its score is for nine.

clue.text: Main centre sharing hospital records

indicators.note: two things sharing one item use it jointly, so the common letter is written only once

blocks.note: arch means chief or main, as in arch-rival
H is the abbreviation for hospital
a hive of activity is a busy centre

explanation.surface: The main hospital site shares its patient records with another centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words for main and centre contain the hospital letter, so they overlap on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a collection of historical records or documents.

clue.text: Appeared to be stitched up by the Speaker

indicators.note: a word spoken by a speaker is heard, not seen, so its sound is what matters

blocks.note: seamed means stitched together

explanation.surface: Someone seemed to be framed by the Speaker of the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitched up' suggests being framed, but it simply means sewn.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemed means gave the impression of being, as appeared to be does.

clue.text: Hint for Philip after cutting cheek – remedial surgery?

blocks.clueFragment: Hint for Philip after cutting cheek
blocks.note: surface reading: a tip for a man named Philip after he cuts his cheek
setter's reading: take the cheek (lip) off Philip, and the three letters left are the answer's first word rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice for Philip after a shaving cut: perhaps he needs corrective surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: PHILIP minus LIP leaves PHI, which is HIP re-placed. The answer also names a common orthopaedic operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hip replacement is surgery to replace a damaged hip joint with an artificial one, a remedial procedure.

clue.text: Country manor remodelled by South American purchasing home

indicators.note: a remodelled building has its parts rearranged, so these letters are reordered
what you purchase you take in and hold, so the jumbled letters take another piece inside them

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation for South American
taken as written, to be rearranged
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A country house is redone by a South American who buys a home there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country manor' reads as one phrase, but country alone is the definition and manor is the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic enclosed by Italy, one of the smallest nations in Europe.

clue.text: Calling hotel, lovely sandwiches

indicators.note: bread sandwiches a filling by enclosing it on both sides, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: nice means lovely
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone phones a hotel that serves lovely sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling' looks like phoning, but it is the noun for a vocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding your niche means finding the role or vocation that suits you, much as a calling does.

clue.text: Collector of precious metals visiting official casually rebuffed

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the word for the official is read backwards
a visitor goes into someone's place, so the metals go inside the official

blocks.note: ref is the casual short form of referee
OR is heraldic gold and AG the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A dealer in gold and silver is turned away by an official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collector of precious metals' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Collector'.
explanation.definitionFit: A forager searches for and gathers things, such as wild food, so is a kind of collector.

clue.text: Digest yogurt regularly and cut wrinkles

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter is kept
cut tells us to trim off the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
lines are wrinkles in the skin

explanation.surface: A diet tip: eating yogurt regularly and cutting down helps smooth out wrinkles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digest' looks like a verb about eating, but it is the noun for a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed summary of information, and an outline is likewise a brief summary.

clue.text: Work zip on Per Una's latest

indicators.note: the latest of anything is the last one, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: zip means nothing, zero, the letter O
taken as written
the last letter of Una

explanation.surface: Someone is fixing the zip on a garment from Per Una, a Marks & Spencer fashion range.
explanation.walkthrough: Per Una is a British clothing label sold by Marks & Spencer; here it is split into PER and the last letter of Una.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for a work, and an opera is a musical and dramatic work.

clue.text: Caught ferret facing partner's animals

indicators.note: caught here means heard, so we want a word that sounds like the next one

blocks.note: to ferret about is to pry; the sound is spelt as in the start of the answer
mate is partner, and mate's (mate is) reads as mates

explanation.surface: A ferret is caught in front of its partner's animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like trapping the ferret, but it means heard. Facing means placed in front of.
explanation.definitionFit: Primates are the order of mammals including apes, monkeys and humans.

clue.text: Supporter raised appeal over charge to show umpire

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising something means reading it from the bottom up

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting garment
it means sex appeal
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A fan raises an appeal against a charge, to show the umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Umpire' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To umpire is to judge a dispute impartially, just as to arbitrate is.

clue.text: Having taken tips, sleek edit tweaked by son flows in the main

indicators.note: tips are the ends, so taking them means removing the first and last letters
something tweaked is adjusted, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, losing its first and last letters
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An editor tidies up a sleek piece of writing, with a son taking tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the open sea, so flows in the main are currents.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee tides are tidal currents running with the wind, flows of water in the sea.

clue.text: Stand in gallery, bored by part right at the end

indicators.note: R stands for right, and being placed at the end means it is moved from the front to the back
something bored by a drill has a hole made in it, so a piece goes inside

blocks.note: the Tate is a famous London gallery
a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: Someone stands in an art gallery, bored by part of the exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries, best known in London. 'Stand' looks like being on your feet, but it means put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to put up with it, which is what tolerate means.

clue.text: Figures old boy lusts after

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to long for is to yearn

explanation.surface: A former pupil fancies some figures, as in attractive bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' suggests bodies or numbers, but it means geometrical shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblongs are rectangles, geometrical figures longer than they are wide.

clue.text: Put coat on lamb as technique to seal?

indicators.note: to seal is to close up inside, so the answer is enclosed within the next words

blocks.note: found across the ends of lamb, as and the start of technique

explanation.surface: A cook asks about the method for coating a roast lamb to lock in its juices.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a definition: basting coats roasting meat to seal in moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste is to spoon fat or juices over meat while it roasts, giving it a coating.

clue.text: One following leading character in Suits' gossip

indicators.note: the leading character is the first one, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of Suits
a gossip is a talker

explanation.surface: A fan of the TV series Suits chats about its main character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading character' suggests the star of the drama, but it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalker is someone who obsessively follows another person.

clue.text: Put down a sandwich served up by my boss

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a sub is a submarine sandwich
the editor is the crossword setter's boss

explanation.surface: Someone sets down a sandwich that their boss brought them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests placing something, but it means insulted.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone down is to belittle or insult them, which abused can mean.

clue.text: With composure, equalise and settle match

blocks.note: first meaning: mental steadiness or poise
second meaning: to make equal or even out; settle and match are further senses

explanation.surface: A footballer calmly equalises and then settles the match.
explanation.walkthrough: This is really a four-way definition: composure, equalise, settle (an account) and match (as weights that balance).
explanation.definitionFit: Balance as a noun is poise or steadiness of mind; as a verb it means to make equal on both sides.

clue.text: Name show enthralling Germany – Bottom?

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
to air is to show or broadcast
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' with a capital looks like Shakespeare's weaver, but it means the lowest point.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of something, its very bottom.

clue.text: Select group of motorists to enter one-time race

indicators.note: to enter a place is to go inside it, so the motorists go within the race

blocks.note: ex means former
the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

clue.text: Fellow taken aback by empty notice board

taken aback is read literally as taken backwards

blocks.note: to spy something is to notice it
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice board' looks like one item, but board is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a governing council of a church, a kind of board of clergy and members.

clue.text: Reserved? Try ditching husband to get dramatic!

blocks.note: a judge will try or hear a case
H is the abbreviation for husband
a marked change is a dramatic one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserved' suggests a shy person, but it means set aside for a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmarked means designated or set aside for a particular use, as reserved can.

clue.text: Prudent time to appear ahead of schedule for individual

indicators.note: arriving ahead of schedule means coming earlier, so that letter moves one place forward

blocks.note: discreet means careful, prudent
T for time names the letter that moves; it is already in the word for prudent, so it adds nothing

explanation.surface: A prudent person makes a point of arriving early for each individual appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the abbreviation for time; in DISCREET it jumps one place earlier, swapping with the final E to turn one word into its soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate and distinct, so each part is individual.

clue.text: Teacher given the sack on reflection remains

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
the sack is slang for bed

explanation.surface: A sacked teacher thinks it over and stays on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given the sack' suggests being fired, but the sack is slang for bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered remains left after something is destroyed.
